properties.description:
SVRABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southeastern Lincoln County in central New Mexico...

* Until 530 PM MDT.

* At 459 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 7 miles southwest
of Tinnie, or 22 miles east of Ruidoso, moving southeast at 5 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Lincoln County.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Heavy rains from severe thunderstorms can produce sudden and
dangerous flows in arroyos, ditches and over low water crossings. Do
not attempt to drive through areas where water covers the roadway.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 28 at 4:13PM MDT until October 28 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
At 413 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of South Central Otero County.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 28 at 5:26PM AST until October 29 at 1:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North facing beaches of Puerto Rico, including Culebra.

* WHEN...Through 1 PM AST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK NOW IN EFFECT THROUGH THURSDAY AFTERNOON

* WHERE...Northern Susitna Valley, including the Parks Highway

* WHEN...From 1 PM Thursday to 2 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult, with low visibility and
rapidly accumulating snow along the Parks Highway.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Light snow will fall overnight tonight through

intensity will then increase during the afternoon hours. The
heaviest snow will fall Thursday night through Friday morning. Snow

an extra flashlight, food and water in your vehicle in case of an
emergency.

accumulations up to two inches and ice accumulation up to one tenth
of an inch.

* WHERE...The Susitna Valley, from around Willow north to the
Talkeetna Spur Road.

* WHEN...From 2 AM to 1 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Thursday morning commute. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Light snow will develop around midnight
tonight. Warmer air aloft will then cause a mix of precipitation
types late tonight through Thursday morning with a general
transition from snow to freezing rain. The willow area, which tends
to hold on to colder surface temperatures has the highest potential
for freezing rain. Surface temperatures will slowly rise above
freezing late Thursday morning through Thursday afternoon, with a
changeover to plain rain.
properties.instruction:

conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San
Francisco Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.

than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 01:43 PM
Thursday 10/29, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 02:39 PM
Friday 10/30, and 1.1 feet above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 03:44
PM on Saturday 10/31. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 01:43 PM
Thursday 10/29, and 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 02:39
PM Friday 10/30. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 28 at 2:42PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

Low pressure begins to dig southward from the PACNW on Friday,
tapping into a fetch of Pacific moisture that will evolve into an
atmospheric river streaming into the Desert Southwest this weekend.
Showers and thunderstorms develop on Friday and Saturday across the
region. Lighter rainfall totals Friday and Saturday will reflect,
initially lower, moisture. However, a few thunderstorms could produce
impactful downpours on saturated soils left over from last weekend's
historic rainfall.

Deeper moisture develops Saturday night and early Sunday. This is
expected to produce heavier and more widespread rainfall across
southeast UT and southwest CO Sunday and Monday, mostly below 10000
feet. While rivers are forecast to remain below action stage, a
growing concern lies in the potential for runoff around saturated
hillsides in the region. This could produce rock, mud, and debris
flows onto roadways, as well as flash flood prone burn scars, washes,
slot canyons, and arroyos. Early estimates predict an area of 1 to 2
inches of new rainfall for portions of southeast UT and southwest CO.

This is a preliminary forecast that hinges on slight shifts in a
strong moisture plume impacting the region. It also attempts to
capture the most statistically likely outcome, despite stronger and
weaker outlier predictions. Outdoor enthusiasts, motorists, and
residents of recent flood impacted areas are encouraged to remain
abreast of the developing forecast in the coming days.

out to 60 nm.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Seas will gradually subside through the
afternoon and evening, but remain steep.
properties.instruction:
A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 21 to 33 knots
and/or seas 10 feet or higher are expected to produce hazardous
wave conditions to small craft. Inexperienced mariners,
especially those operating smaller vessels should avoid
navigating in these conditions.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 28 at 4:40PM EDT by NWS Burlington VT
properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA...Most of Vermont, except the Connecticut River
Valley and parts of southern Vermont.

* WINDS...Southwest 5 to 15 mph with gusts 20 to 35 mph, highest
in the Champlain Valley.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 45 to 50 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...60 to 65 degrees.

* FUELS...Per coordination with our partners, the recent dry
weather has caused leaf litter, across the region to dry out.

* IMPACTS...If any fires were to start the weather and fuel
conditions could cause fires to quickly get out of control and
be difficult to contain.

For more information about the current fire danger rating, any burn
restrictions, and wildfire prevention and education, please visit
your state forestry or environmental protection website.
